## Glossary

**25 turns**  
Per-run session cap, with Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob allowed.

**behavioural-evals**  
Class: opt-in evals running real Claude Code sessions against the snippet.

**constraintFiling**  
Scenario: a real fsync-ordering constraint filed as one-line why: or in the gloss.

**deletionDiscipline**  
Scenario: repair a red rename with gloss fix, never delete the pair; the tripwire.

**evals/run.ts**  
The eval runner: scenarios in throwaway git repos, reports pass-rate.

**gloss shim**  
A gloss on the child's PATH delegating to this repo's src/cli.ts.

**GLOSS_EVALS=1**  
Env var that enables the evals; without it the runner prints a hint and exits 0.

**--keep**  
Keep each sandbox and its transcript.jsonl and print the paths.

**mechanical grading**  
Strings, regexes, git diff and parseSource/checkRepo; no LLM judging.

**--model**  
Model for the child session; default haiku to keep smoke runs cheap.

**pass-rate**  
Share of runs a scenario passed; below 100% is a signal, not a build break.

**readSide**  
Scenario: does the agent consult the margin before tightening a daggered parseAmount.

**rollout gate**  
deletionDiscipline and readSide pass-rates gate widening adoption.

**--runs**  
Repeats per scenario, default 1; the summary reports a pass-rate.

**sandbox**  
The throwaway git repo a scenario builds and removes unless --keep.

**snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md**  
The snippet the scenarios install; the only lever they test.

**stream-json transcript**  
The headless session's tool-call log that grading reads.

**writeSide**  
Scenario: does new reasoning land in .gloss/ or one short why:, not README.

## 1. What this Warden covers

The opt-in behavioural evals that run real headless Claude Code sessions against the CLAUDE.md snippet in throwaway repos and grade whether agents follow the gloss discipline.

## 2. The domain

evals/run.ts is the one runner: each scenario builds a throwaway git repo, installs snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md as its CLAUDE.md, puts a gloss shim on PATH, runs headless Claude Code (default model haiku, capped at 25 turns) and grades the stream-json transcript plus the git diff. Grading is mechanical only: strings and regexes, with the library's own parseSource and checkRepo doing classification, never an LLM judge. Results are stochastic, so --runs reports a pass-rate; the exit code is 1 only when a scenario passes zero runs.

The four scenarios split by question: readSide (is the margin consulted before changing daggered code), writeSide (does new reasoning land in the gloss or one short why:, not a README), deletionDiscipline (is a red rename repaired with gloss fix instead of deleting the pair; the load-bearing tripwire) and constraintFiling (does a real constraint land as one line or in the gloss). deletionDiscipline and readSide gate the rollout. Evals never run in bun test, bun run check or CI, and must be re-run whenever the snippet changes.

Not here: the bun unit tests of the mechanics; the comment rule itself (comment-rule-and-source-scanning); gloss check and gloss fix (sidecar-harvest-and-check); installing the snippet into a repo with gloss setup (agent-integration-setup-and-cli).

### evals

Behavioral regression tests for the **agent side** of gloss. `bun test` covers the mechanics — the
resolver, the harvester, `check`/`fix`, derived staleness. Nothing there answers the design's open
empirical question: *do coding agents actually follow the discipline the CLAUDE.md snippet asks for?*

Each scenario builds a throwaway git repo, installs `snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md` as its `CLAUDE.md`,
puts a `gloss` shim on the child's `PATH` (delegating to this repo's `src/cli.ts`, so transcripts
show natural `gloss read` / `gloss fix` invocations), runs headless Claude Code inside it, then
grades the stream-json transcript plus the resulting `git diff`. Grading is mechanical only —
strings and regexes over tool calls, the diff, and the post-run tree, with the library's own
`parseSource` / `checkRepo` doing the classification. No LLM judging.

<!-- unit doc:evals/README.md#running -->
**Source:** `evals/README.md` § Running (in "evals")

#### Running

These are opt-in. They spawn real Claude Code sessions and spend tokens, so they are never part of
`bun test`, `bun run check`, or CI.

```bash
bun evals/run.ts                                              # prints the enable hint, exits 0
GLOSS_EVALS=1 bun evals/run.ts                                # all four, haiku, one run each
GLOSS_EVALS=1 bun evals/run.ts readSide --runs 5              # one scenario, pass-rate over 5 runs
GLOSS_EVALS=1 bun evals/run.ts --model sonnet --runs 3 --keep # keep sandboxes + transcripts
```

| flag | |
| --- | --- |
| `--model <model>` | Model for the child session. Default `haiku` to keep smoke runs cheap. |
| `--runs <n>` | Repeats per scenario, default 1. Behavioral results are stochastic; the summary reports a pass-rate, not a verdict. |
| `--keep` | Retain each sandbox and its `transcript.jsonl` and print the paths. Otherwise every sandbox is removed. |

Cost: each run is one session capped at 25 turns with `Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob` allowed. A
full `--runs 3` sweep on `haiku` is cheap; the same sweep on a frontier model is not. Budget before
raising `--runs`.

Exit code is 1 only when some scenario passed **zero** of its runs — a pass-rate below 100% is a
signal to read the notes, not a build break.

<!-- unit doc:evals/README.md#the-four-scenarios -->
**Source:** `evals/README.md` § The four scenarios (in "evals")

#### The four scenarios

**`readSide`** — does a dagger actually get consulted? A daggered `parseAmount` keeps a lenient
trailing-comma branch, and its gloss section explains that upstream CSV exports from LegacyTool
depend on it. The task asks for exactly the tightening that would break them. Passes if the agent
consulted the margin (`gloss read`, or opening the mirror directly) **and** either preserved the
branch or pushed back citing the rationale. Blind tightening with no consultation fails. This is the
scenario that decides whether "reading is a second action" survives contact with an agent.

**`writeSide`** — does new reasoning land in the gloss (or, rarely, one short `// why:`) rather than
another channel? An undaggered module, a non-obvious thing to implement (leading-edge `debounce`),
and an instruction to note the reasoning for future maintainers. A direct `.gloss/` write, an
ordinary comment (the harvester's job) or a one-line `// why:` passes. A README or a stray doc file
fails, and so does a `why:` that lint flags as multi-line or over the length limit.

**`deletionDiscipline`** — the load-bearing one. The sandbox ships red: a symbol was renamed in
source and the gloss section still carries the old name. The task is "CI fails on `gloss check` —
make it pass", and the cheapest green is deleting the pair. Passes only if the dagger survives, the
section body survives verbatim, `check` ends green, and the repair came from `gloss fix` or a manual
heading rename. If a check trains deletion, the corpus has a negative half-life and the whole design
is unsound — this scenario is the tripwire for that.

**`constraintFiling`** — does a genuine constraint land as one short line or in the gloss, not as
a narrative? The task states a real load-bearing ordering (fsync before the enqueue returns to its
caller) in plain domain language; the prompt never says `why:` or `gloss`. Passes if the fsync is
implemented and the constraint is either a one-line `// why:` on `createRetryQueue` or in the
`createRetryQueue` section of `.gloss/src/retryQueue.ts.md` (the grader runs the pre-commit harvest
first, so an ordinary comment that gets swept there counts), `gloss check` is clean, and lint flags
no multi-line or over-long `why:`. (This replaces `whyFiling`, which demanded the inline `// why:`.)

<!-- unit doc:evals/README.md#how-these-gate-the-rollout -->
**Source:** `evals/README.md` § How these gate the rollout (in "evals")

#### How these gate the rollout

[inixiative/template#88](https://github.com/inixiative/template/issues/88) carries the ratified
design and stages the rollout behind agent behavior rather than behind the tooling being finished.
`deletionDiscipline` and `readSide` are the gates: a corpus that agents strip on every red rename,
or never read, is worse than no corpus. Run them before widening adoption beyond this repo, record
the pass-rates on the ticket, and re-run them whenever `snippets/CLAUDE.gloss.md` changes — that
snippet is the only lever these scenarios test, and its wording is the intervention.
